title: Ekpili (seed-shell rattle)
summary: The ekpili is a string of dried, hollowed seed halves worn on the ankles or waist by Igbo dancers as a rhythmic rattle. Fresh seeds are halved and cleared out, the shells are strung together, and they clack against each other as the dancer steps.
howToPlay: Three places are lit on the hanging strands: Flick near the bar, Sway through the middle, Clack at the lowest shells.
The strands swing and the shells knock together when a stroke sounds.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Let the clacks follow the step.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: It is a dancer's rattle: every step shakes the strings of shells and adds a dry clatter to the music of the feet.
credits: Tradition: the ekpili; patterns written for this game
